parameters.content:
## 🏠 Property Search + Owner & Value Analysis — Searchbug (api_prop)

Look up property records by address, parcel ID or owner name — one at a time or in bulk from a CSV — then work out the things people actually open county records for: **who lives there, what the land is worth per acre, and how long the owner has held it.**

### How it works
1. **Single:** pick a Search Type and enter what to search for plus the county/state. **Bulk:** leave What blank and upload a CSV (what, location, search_type).
2. Validate Input drops rows with no search value or an unrecognized type; Dedupe Searches removes repeat rows so the same parcel is never paid for twice.
3. The API call retries 3× and is throttled to 1 request/second. Check Results routes empty and failed responses to No Results.
4. Score Property Value derives, for every parcel:
   • **OWNER_OCCUPIED** — does the tax bill go to the property itself, or somewhere else? Compares the mailing address against the physical address.
   • **OUT_OF_STATE_OWNER** — mailing state vs property state.
   • **VALUE_PER_ACRE**, **LAND_VALUE_PCT**, **IMPROVEMENT_PCT**, **IS_VACANT_LAND**.
   • **SALE_VS_MARKET_PCT** — last sale price against current market value.
   • **YEARS_SINCE_SALE** — how long the current owner has held it.
   • **LEAD_SCORE 0–100 → LEAD_TIER HOT / WARM / COLD** and **FLAGS**: ABSENTEE_OWNER, OUT_OF_STATE_OWNER, VACANT_LAND, LONG_HELD, SOLD_BELOW_MARKET, ADJACENT_PARCEL_SAME_OWNER.
5. Two sheets are written:
   • **Property Search** — one row per parcel: all 47 county fields plus the 19 derived ones
   • **PS Summary** — one row per search: parcels found, total and average market value, total acreage, average value per acre, absentee / out-of-state / vacant counts, best lead.

### How to set up
- [ ] Add your Searchbug CO_CODE + PASS in the HTTP Request (Body Parameters)
- [ ] Connect your OWN Google Sheets account in BOTH Save nodes
- [ ] Point them at your own spreadsheet and create two tabs:
      • "Property Search" (66 columns — see Save Property Detail)
      • "PS Summary" (16 columns — see Save Search Summary)
- [ ] Activate and share the form link

### Search types
Property Address → SRCH = A · Parcel ID → SRCH = P · Owner's Name → SRCH = O
CSV rows may use the full label, the letter, or leave search_type blank to fall back to the form's dropdown.

### Lead score
Absentee owner +30 · out-of-state owner +15 · held 15+ years +25 (8+ years +10) · vacant land +10 · land is 70%+ of value +10 · adjacent parcel same owner +10. HOT ≥ 65, WARM ≥ 35.

Change any of it at the top of Score Property Value — the weights are plain numbers.

## 1. Single or Bulk Input

Single or Bulk? checks whether the What field was filled. Single → straight to Normalize Input; CSV upload → Extract CSV first.

Normalize Input standardizes the column names, so a CSV can use what / search / query / address / parcel_id / owner_name for the search value and location / county / state for the place.

## 2. Map, Validate & Dedupe

Set Search Input turns the search type into the Searchbug code — it accepts "Property Address", "address" or plain "A", so a hand-written CSV works.

Validate Input then requires a search value and a recognized type; anything else returns an Invalid Input message instead of failing the run.

Dedupe Searches collapses identical searches into one call and stamps each with a SEARCH_ID that follows it into both sheets.

## 3. Search & Route

The API node retries 3× and sends 1 request per second, so a long CSV finishes instead of tripping rate limits.

Check Results only passes a response that really has a parcel in it. Attach Search Context carries the SEARCH_ID past the API call and turns Data.PROPERTY into an array — Searchbug returns a bare object when there is exactly one match, which is why the plain field mapping in v1 came back blank whenever a search returned several parcels.

## 4. Flatten & Analyse

Flatten Properties makes one row per parcel and pulls all 47 county fields, including the nested LAND_COVER and CROP_COVER counts.

Score Property Value then derives the analysis layer — owner occupancy, out-of-state owner, value per acre, land vs improvement split, sale price against market value, years since the last sale, and a HOT / WARM / COLD lead tier with flags.

## ⚠️ 5. Two Outputs

**Save Property Detail** — one row per parcel, 66 columns: the 19 derived fields first, then all 47 original county fields.

**Save Search Summary** — one row per search: parcels found, total and average market value, total acreage, average value per acre, absentee / out-of-state / vacant land counts, best lead score and tier, and the largest-value owner.

Connect your OWN Google Sheets credential in both and create the tabs with matching row-1 headers.

Don't click ⋮ → Refresh — it erases the column mapping.
